candidates.summary: publishedKinds cuts the ExtensionKindsUpTo(limit) window before dropping view-less hooks, so a view-less hook registered first hides published kinds from the badges and the register event, and lets Register past its maxEventKinds guard
candidates.failure_scenario: Issuer registers one view-less hook (RegisterExtension(h, nil)) and then 9 published views: Render(key) shows 8 badges and no ellipsis, though GetExtensionKinds returns 9. With 9 view-less hooks then 1 view, the page says _core only_. With 1 view-less hook then 17 views, Register succeeds (no 'too many extensions') and the register event lists 16 of 17 kinds, which an indexer reads as complete. The 953cd82e5 Collection counted views only (avl of views), so this is new in this round's refactor.

candidates.summary: Token.ExtensionView is a linear scan of the extension slice, and publishedKinds calls it once per kind, so grc721reg.GetExtensionKinds costs O(n^2) in an extension count the issuer sets, extensions added after Register included
candidates.failure_scenario: An issuer registers its collection, then attaches n view-bearing extensions (the registry keeps the live token, so the maxEventKinds cap never sees them). Every GetExtensionKinds(key) by another realm then walks ExtensionKindsUpTo(0) and does a lookupExtension per kind: read cost 12.6M gas at n=100, 38.7M at 200, 134.2M at 400, 481.8M at 800 (ratio per doubling 3.1, 3.5, 3.6, tending to 4). The 953cd82e5 Collection held views in an avl.Tree, so lookup was O(log n) and the read linear.
candidates.verify_by: cp tests/b2-reach-kinds-quadratic.gno into examples/gno.land/r/demo/defi/grc721reg/zz_reach_quad_test.gno; cd examples && gno test ./gno.land/r/demo/defi/grc721reg -run TestReachQuad -v; read cost = GAS(Read<n>) - GAS(Setup<n>), linear would double per doubling

candidates.summary: RegisterExtension accepts the hook itself as its view, which hands its exported OnMint/OnTransfer/OnBurn to every realm through Token.ExtensionView and grc721reg.GetExtension; the registry tests use exactly that shape
candidates.failure_scenario: An issuer copies grc721reg_test.gno:277/355/502 and calls ledger.RegisterExtension(x, x) with a stateful hook. Any realm then does GetExtension(key, kind), asserts the result to grc721.Extension and calls OnMint/OnBurn directly; the write commits under the issuer's realm by borrow rule, corrupting the extension's state without a ledger operation. Before this PR no hook was reachable from *Token. The in-tree royalty, metadata and enumerable keep hook and view distinct.
